The '''Supercopa Peruana''', ''(Peruvian Supercup)'' is a football competition organized by the [[Peruvian Football Federation]] since 2020. It is played in a single match, on a neutral field, which, if necessary, breaks the tie with shots from the penalty spot. It is played between the champions of the [[Copa Bicentenario]] and [[Peruvian Primera División]]. In the event that the same team wins both the cup and the championship, its opponent will be the runner-up of the latter.
== History ==
===Background===
In 1919, the Liga Peruana de Football, now known as the [[Professional Football Sports Association|Asociación Deportiva de Fútbol Profesional]], established a super cup reserved for First Division champions. Club [[Alianza Lima]], champions of the [[1919 Liga Peruana de Football]], won the [[Copa de Campeones del Perú|Copa de Campeones del Perú “Felipe Ríos”]] after defeating [[Jorge Chávez No. 1|Jorge Chávez N°1]], champions of the [[1913 Liga Peruana de Football]], by a score of 2–0.

In 2012, the [[Peruvian Football Federation]] revived the super cup format under the name [[2012 Copa Federación|Copa Federación]]. The match was contested between [[José Gálvez FBC|José Gálvez]], champions of the [[2011 Torneo Intermedio]], and Club [[Juan Aurich]], champions of the [[2011 Torneo Descentralizado|2011 Peruvian Primera División]]. The club from Chimbote won 1–0 and was crowned champion.

Later, in 2018, the [[Professional Football Sports Association|Asociación Deportiva de Fútbol Profesional]], with sponsorship from [[Movistar]], organized a new version of the competition called the [[2018 Supercopa Movistar]]. The tournament was played between [[Alianza Lima]], champions of the [[2017 Torneo Descentralizado]], and [[Sport Boys]], champions of the [[2017 Peruvian Segunda División]]. The title was won by Alianza Lima after a 1–0 victory.

===Liga de Fútbol Profesional===
The [[Peruvian Football Federation]] took control of the local domestic league from the [[Professional Football Sports Association]], the tournament organizers, in 2019 and announced that the Peruvian first division tournament would be re-branded for 2019.<ref>{{cite web |title=FPF ANUNCIA LA CREACIÓN DE UNA NUEVA LIGA DE FÚTBOL PROFESIONAL |url=http://www.fpf.org.pe/fpf-anuncia-creacion-nueva-liga-futbol-profesional/ |website=fpf.org.pe |publisher=Federación Peruana de Fútbol |access-date=8 February 2020 |language=es}}</ref> With this re-branding, the tournament was expanded from 16 to 18 teams and then to 20 in 2020. Also, The [[Peruvian Segunda División|second division]] tournament was re-branded as Liga 2.

The Peruvian Football Federation also announced the creation of a new domestic cup tournament to be played once a year by both the first and second division teams, the winner of which would receive a berth to the [[Copa Sudamericana]]. The new domestic cup tournament was named [[Copa Bicentenario]] in honor of Peru's bicentennial.<ref>{{cite web |last1=LR |first1=Redacción |title=La Liga 1, un nuevo reto para el fútbol peruano |url=https://larepublica.pe/marketing/1398795-liga-1-nuevo-reto-futbol-peruano/ |website=larepublica.pe |publisher=La República |access-date=8 February 2020 |language=es |date=29 May 2019}}</ref> In 2020, the Peruvian Football Federation announced the creation of a [[super cup]] between the Copa Bicentenario champion and the Liga 1 champion to serve as a  "[[Curtain raiser|curtain-raiser]]" to the season. The name of the new tournament is Supercopa Peruana, ''Peruvian Super Cup'', which is expected to be played in January of every year before the start of the regular season tournaments.<ref>{{cite web |title=FPF: Presentó nuevo formato de Liga 1 para la temporada 2020 |url=https://libero.pe/futbol-peruano/liga-1/1528619-liga-1-2020-sera-campeonato-nacional-ano-cupo-extranjeros-bolsa-minutos-fpf-copa-libertadores-alianza-lima-universitario-twitter-foto/5?ref=notagaleria |website=libero.pe |publisher=Libero |access-date=8 February 2020 |language=es}}</ref>

[[Escuela Municipal Deportivo Binacional|Binacional]] and [[Atlético Grau]] played the first edition of the new Super Cup tournament in 2020. Atlético Grau defeated Binacional by 3–0 to win the 3rd title in its history.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Depor |first1=Redacción |title=¡Goleó al campeón nacional! Atlético Grau se coronó campeón de la Supercopa 2020 al ganarle 3-0 a Binacional [VIDEO] |url=https://depor.com/futbol-peruano/descentralizado/binacional-vs-atletico-grau-en-vivo-online-via-golperu-por-la-supercopa-peruana-2020-nczd-noticia/ |website=Depor |access-date=8 February 2020 |language=es |date=23 January 2020}}</ref>
